title: Scaling Up: How a Few Companies Make It...and Why the Rest Don't (Rockefeller Habits 2.0 Revised Edition)
author: Verne Harnish
primary_purpose: To provide a practical, actionable framework and set of tools for business leaders to successfully scale their organizations while avoiding common growth pitfalls, based on time-tested practices inspired by Rockefeller habits.

structure_format.organization: Organized around four key decision areas—People, Strategy, Execution, and Cash—each with step-by-step frameworks, checklists, and real-world case studies
features: Scalable one-page tools (One Page Strategic Plan, People tools, etc.)
Case studies from successful high-growth firms

key_concepts_lessons: The importance of disciplined focus on People, Strategy, Execution, and Cash for scaling up.
Leadership needs to evolve at every stage of company growth.
Clear communication, accountability, and regular meeting rhythms are essential for alignment.
Building scalable systems and processes prevents chaos as a company grows.
Financial discipline and predictable cash flow are critical for sustainable growth.
Culture, talent, and effective hiring practices underpin successful scaling.
Critical thinking tools (like the One Page Strategic Plan) bring clarity and alignment.
notable_features: Rockefeller Habits 2.0—an updated set of habits inspired by John D. Rockefeller’s management principles
One Page Strategic Plan template recognized globally
Step-by-step toolkits for every growth area
Emphasis on real-world company stories and applied learning
Widely adopted by the Gazelles business coaching community
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of renewed interest in entrepreneurship and startup scaling, 'Scaling Up' built upon the original 'Mastering the Rockefeller Habits' by codifying actionable systems for fast-growing companies in the digital age. It reflects the shift from solo entrepreneurship to team-based, high-growth organizations.
reception_impact: International bestseller, influential in business education and accelerator programs
Praised for demystifying the complexities of scaling an organization
Highly valued by business coaches, VCs, and founders for its practicality and structure
Critics occasionally note the framework may require adaptation for very early-stage startups or non-traditional organizations
